key_insight: SpatialBench provides a holistic evaluation revealing that current spatial foundation models are not universally 'all-round' — they excel in some settings but show consistent failure modes across unseen viewpoints, domain shifts, input densities, and hardware constraints.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a unified, comprehensive benchmark for measuring spatial foundation model generalization and robustness across diverse downstream tasks, arbitrary viewpoints, varying scene domains, input densities, and deployment hardware constraints.
method: Assemble a diverse benchmark suite spanning multiple downstream tasks (e.g., 3D perception, localization, scene understanding) with both real-world and synthetic datasets.
Introduce controlled stress tests: viewpoint and domain shifts, systematic input-density variations, and hardware/resource-constrained evaluation protocols.
Define standardized metrics and evaluation protocols to produce comparable per-model profiles and identify consistent strengths and weaknesses.
impact: Gives researchers and practitioners a practical, standardized tool to diagnose where spatial models fail, prioritize improvements, and make informed choices for deployment in real-world, resource-constrained, or cross-domain settings.
visual_elements: Radar chart comparing models across key axes (tasks, viewpoint robustness, domain generalization, input-density tolerance, hardware efficiency).
Heatmap matrix of model × task × domain showing performance gaps and failure hotspots.
Flow diagram of the benchmark pipeline: datasets → perturbations (viewpoint/domain/density) → evaluation metrics → diagnostic reports.
Bar charts showing performance degradation under reduced input density and limited hardware (latency/throughput vs. accuracy).
paper_title: SpatialBench: Is Your Spatial Foundation Model an All-Round Player?
paper_authors: Haosong Peng, Hao Li, Jiaqi Chen, Yuhao Pan, Runmao Yao
